package.name: som-app
package.rule: The npm package name is always som-app. The prompt package name appears only in the src/schema.ts header comment. So package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json and every other fixed file are the same bytes for every product.

service.rule: The React product is a front end for the Python service that the same prompt generates without a target (or with target python). It calls only the routes in scope.json routes.api_calls and reads only the response bodies that the Python service returns for them.
service.proxy: vite.config.ts sends /api/* to SOM_API_URL with the /api prefix removed, in both the dev server and vite preview. SOM_API_URL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000. The built dist is static; serving it with a reverse proxy for /api is outside phase 1.
service.errors: src/api.ts maps every response to Result<T>. A status other than the expected one is an ApiError with the response detail when it is a string; a 422 detail array becomes fieldErrors for loc ["body", <field name>] and otherErrors ("<loc joined by .>: <msg>") for every other item. A fetch that throws is status 0 with detail "network error".

execution.rule: Vite builds and serves the TypeScript sources; vitest runs the tests in jsdom; tsc -p tsconfig.json is a type-check gate only (noEmit). Node and the vendored packages in toolchain.json are the only tools.
execution.erasable_syntax_only: Sources use only syntax that type stripping can erase: no enum, no namespace, no parameter properties, no decorators. tsconfig.json sets erasableSyntaxOnly.
execution.imports: Relative imports name the .ts or .tsx file. Type-only imports use import type, as verbatimModuleSyntax requires.
execution.react: Function components and hooks only. React Router in declarative mode: BrowserRouter in src/main.tsx, Routes in src/App.tsx. No data router, loader, action or server rendering.

files.rule: Bytes equal reference/package-lock.json, written by the one approved npm download (toolchain.json packages).
Bytes equal reference/vite.config.ts: the /api proxy (service.proxy) and the jsdom test environment.
Bytes equal reference/src/main.tsx: mounts App in BrowserRouter and StrictMode on #root.
Bytes equal reference/src/App.tsx: the routes of scope.json routes.pages.
Bytes equal reference/src/api.ts: the fetch client (service.errors).
Bytes equal reference/src/spec.ts: the types of the constants in src/schema.ts.
Bytes equal reference/src/form.ts: form text to JSON values and the bodies sent on create and edit.
Bytes equal reference/src/app.test.tsx: page tests against a fake fetch, driven by the constants in src/schema.ts.
Bytes equal render_reference.py schema_ts for the prompt: the Row, CreateBody, PatchBody and ListQuery types, and the RESOURCE, FIELDS and QUERY constants typed by src/spec.ts.
Bytes equal render_reference.py readme for the prompt: the resource name and path, the run and check commands, the pages and the field table.

renderer.rule: The Rust renderer gives the same bytes as render_reference.py render(prompt) for every in-scope prompt. The generated files are already in the formatter's output, so prettier --check accepts them unchanged; the formatter does not run during compile or assemble.

spec.required: A required field has nullable false and no default.
spec.optional: An optional field has default equal to the prompt default, or null when the prompt has none (v1 and v2), and nullable true exactly when the default is null.
spec.query: v1 has QUERY null. v2 to v4 have filter {field: filter_field, param: filter_value for v2 or the field name for v3 and v4, type: the field type}, before: date_field or null, pageSize 20, maxLimit: query.max_limit.
spec.timestamps: RESOURCE.timestamps is true for v3 and v4.

limits.rule: At most 19 files, 1 to 64 blocks per file (bundle schema), and at most 64 blocks in total across files (planning, SCOPE_TOO_LARGE; assemble, INVALID_SCHEMA). Every fixed file is one block; package-lock.json counts as one file and one block.

naming.typescript_items: Variable, function, type, component, module and file names come from the fixed files. No TypeScript identifier comes from the prompt.
naming.fields: A field name is an unquoted member of the Row, CreateBody, PatchBody and ListQuery type literals (always an IdentifierName under the compiler-v1 pattern) and a JSON string literal elsewhere. Records keyed by prompt names are read only through own() in src/form.ts (Object.hasOwn).
naming.reserved: __proto__, constructor and prototype are refused by scope.json identifier_reserved.
